newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower but buoyed by cash basis.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower but buoyed by cash basis.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended lower but closed relatively higher than their counterparts in Chicago thanks to strong domestic mill demand for HRW wheat, traders said.

"The domestic cash market was on fire. Our spot cash basis in Kansas City traded seven to nine cents (per bushel) higher," a KCBT trader said. "People were also buying Kansas City, selling Chicago, blowing out of their short-Kansas City, long-Chicago positions in which they were losing money."
The KCBT/CBOT Dec spread widened Thursday to 42-1/4 cents per bushel from 28-3/4 cents.
Traders also noted the traded KCBT Dec/March inverse widened to 25-1/2 cents late, after opening at 20 cents.

KCBT wheat closed one to 6-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with Dec down one cent at $4.26-1/4. New contract lows were set in March, May, July and September 1997. March ended five cents lower at $4.01-1/4, just above its new low at $4.00-1/2.
U.S. wheat was pressured throughout the session by poor wheat exports and by the International Grains Council's upward revision of its world wheat production forecast.
The EU's move Thursday to nearly double wheat export subsidies also hit U.S. wheat values.

Volumes were heavy, with CIS buying 2.4 million Dec bushels and selling 3.4 million March and 1.4 million July. Man International bought 2.6 million March and 1.3 million Dec, traders said. FIMAT sold two million Dec bushels for the second consecutive session.
